I would try to explain it. Say you have a text block: "I love Voat. It is the best! It promotes free speech." Now you converted to lower case before storing in database field: "i love voat. it is the best! it promotes free speech." Next, you construct a string matching query "I love Voat" and try to search in postgresql database. It will try to find "i love voat" == "I love Voat", which is obviously not an exact match. And so it returns empty entry.

But if you convert both to lowercase or uppercase, it will either be "i love voat" == "i love voat", or "I LOVE VOAT" == "I LOVE VOAT", which is true since they are now identical string. What the ILIKE query does is it will do a string matching by converting it to lowercase. Therefore, it won't matter whether it's a mix of upper/lowercase letters.
